edits.value_json: 听 is the standardized simplified form of 聽, meaning “hear” or “listen.” Its current left–right structure is 口 and 斤. The same split appears in the received analysis of an older use meaning “smiling appearance,” but does not establish how 听 came to represent 聽.
口 is the left-hand component in the current form. In the received analysis of the older smiling-word use, it depicts a mouth contributing to the expression.
斤 is the right-hand component in the current form. The received analysis assigns it a sound role for the older smiling-word use; this does not establish why 听 came to represent 聽.

The received Shuowen entry analyzes 听 in its older “smiling appearance” use as 口 with 斤 as phonetic. The curated image is identified as a modern redraw of a 聽 form in Shuowen small-seal style; it does not depict the older 听 graph or establish a sequence of graphic changes.

verified_uncited_book_records.text: The 聽 entry’s historical sequence is labeled 商, 西周, 戰國, 說文小篆, 漢, then clerical forms. The author analyzes the oracle-bone and bronze forms as associative, with ear and mouth representing speech received by the ear, and describes the received Shuowen account as adding 悳 as a sound element. The continuation discusses extensions from hearing to accepting/obeying, inquiry/governance, and waiting. It then says 聽 is now simplified to 听, separately identified with the Shuowen 口-plus-斤 analysis and smiling sense. These are the author’s analyses; the scan does not establish every proposed historical relationship.
